The *Pubbapetādisapañha* ("Offerings To the Dead", Mil 6.3.4) is a chapter in the *Milindapañha* dealing with the efficacy and reception of offerings dedicated to deceased ancestors [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral notes its thematic and doctrinal connection to the *Jāṇussoṇisutta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 10.177), which similarly addresses whether departed relatives receive gifts offered on their behalf [SuttaCentral].
SuttaCentral does not catalog curated canonical parallels in other languages, though it lists three modern translations across three languages [SuttaCentral]. According to automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus, the text shares 301 passages with 24 other Pali works [DharmaNexus]. The vast majority of these internal overlaps occur within other discussions of the *Milindapañha*, demonstrating recurrent dialogue structures and formulaic phrasing; its most extensive reuse partners include the *Akālamaraṇapañha* (Mil 6.3.6), *Dhammābhisamayapañha* (Mil 6.3.8), *Bhavantasaṅkhārajāyamānapañha* (Mil 3.3.5), and *Vāyāmakaraṇapañha* (Mil 3.4.5), alongside shared canonical phrasings with the *Kusalattika* of the *Paṭṭhāna* [DharmaNexus]. Across languages, DharmaNexus identifies low-to-moderate machine alignments with Chinese *Ekottarika-āgama* material (T 125) and Tibetan translations of Mahāyāna works, notably the *Amitābhavyūhasūtra* (D 49) and the *Saṅghāṭīsūtra* (D 102) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
